messages:
incident-bot: Paging: GPU instability detected on host pool 'infer-prod-1' — 8 nodes reporting driver-reset/Xid spikes > threshold (alert_id: gpu.xid.surge.3005). Please acknowledge with /ack.
alice (oncall): acked. I'm pulling up dashboards now. SLA impact? :eyes:
ben (sre): seeing sudden tail of driver resets on nodes infer-prod-1-[05..12], Xid 31 mostly, some Xid 43. Containers are restarting; a couple of model-serving pods hit OOM after restart.
carla (runtime): confirming, our runtime logs show repeated "GPU reset detected - NVML: Xid 31" then container crash loops. Fallback routing kicked in for some routes but not all.
maria (support): we have two customer tickets open mentioning elevated error rates and timeouts for embeddings. I can correlate request IDs if needed.
alice (oncall): immediate action: isolate the noisy nodes. Ben, can you cordon node set and start drain? We should avoid mass evacs that cause capacity OOM everywhere.
ben (sre): on it. Commanding:
```
kubectl cordon infer-prod-1-05
kubectl drain infer-prod-1-05 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --grace-period=60
``` 
ben (sre): draining 05 now. Will drain 06..08 sequentially and monitor.
carla (runtime): switching canary routing to model-variant-low-gpu for 10% traffic to avoid high mem pressure. Updating routing policy.
todd (prod-eng): any signs of ECC errors (uncorrectable) or just Xid? ECC would imply hardware fault.
ben (sre): nvml shows ECC corrected spikes on 06 and 09; not many uncorrectable yet. dmesg on host shows:
```
[ 1234.567890] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 31, pid=21456, GPU has fallen off the bus.
[ 1234.568000] nvidia-gpu 0000:65:00.0: GPU has fallen off the bus.
```
carla (runtime): container logs show OOM killer invoked after driver-reset and restart churn:
```
RuntimeError: cuda out of memory
  at runtime/serving/session.py:142
```
alice (oncall): are we seeing correlated host reboots or just driver resets? infra-bot, what does the fleet telemetry say?
infra-bot: Fleet telemetry: no automated reboots. Kernel stays up; only nvidia modules logging resets. Driver version: 525.85.12 across pool.
ben (sre): draining 05,06,07 now. 08 still active, but error rate on 08 is trending up.
maria (support): customer-ops reported increased 5xx for embeddings between 16:05-16:12 UTC. I'll open bridge if we need to call out customers.
alice (oncall): initial impact estimate: ~4.7% of inference requests failed or timed out during spike window; primary affected: embeddings & short-text generation. Need a P0 comms if this expands.
carla (runtime): immediate mitigations applied: prefix KV-cache warming disabled on affected model to reduce mem usage; lower batch size for incoming requests for fallback variant; automatic fallback to CPU-lites for non-latency-critical jobs.
ben (sre): quick health check across pool:
```
nvidia-smi -q | grep -E "Xid|ECC"
```
Results: 05: Xid 31 x18 in last 10m, ECC corrected count +240; 06: Xid 31 x4, ECC corrected +90; 09: Xid 43 x2.
alice (oncall): good. Ben, keep draining sequentially and cordon. Avoid draining more than 2 nodes concurrently to prevent capacity crunch.
ben (sre): understood. Also triggering kernel module reload on node 09 (non-drained) for test:
```
systemctl stop kubelet
rmmod nvidia_uvm
modprobe nvidia_uvm
systemctl start kubelet
``` 
ben (sre): performed on 09 — driver resets stopped on that host for now; pods recovered. But we'll monitor for recurrence.
todd (prod-eng): does runtime have soft-eviction logic to avoid OOM loops during driver-reset storms? If not, add a backoff.
carla (runtime): there is a backoff but it resets quickly when pods come up; we'll implement a short jittered backoff and disable aggressive prefetch/caching on restart. Pushing a runtime patch to limit retry churn.
alice (oncall): logging action items: cordon+drain noisy nodes, patch runtime backoff, route 10% to low-gpu variant, open customer bridge if impact >5% sustained, collect nvme/dmesg logs and support ticket attachments.
maria (support): opening bridge now and posting initial note to customers with affected regions. :loudspeaker:
maria (support): posted to tickets: "We're actively investigating GPU driver resets affecting a subset of inference hosts; we've applied routing mitigations and are draining impacted machines. ETA for next update: 20m." 
carla (runtime): pushing config change to routing service. Snippet:
```
route: embeddings-v2
fallback: embeddings-v2-cpu-lite
traffic_split: 90/10
``` 
alice (oncall): can we isolate whether this is workload-triggered? Pattern look at request traces around Xid events?
ben (sre): correlating... preliminary: Xid bursts align with larger multi-sequence requests (seq_len > 4096) and an increase in batch size from one customer spike. Not conclusive.
carla (runtime): enabling request tracing for affected nodes; will capture request IDs for matching to customer traces. This will help prove workload correlation.
ben (sre): drained nodes 05-08 sequentially. 05 had highest corrected ECC counts; plan: keep cordoned and schedule hardware RMA after triage. 06 showed lower but increasing trend; keeping cordoned.
alice (oncall): are there any pods still crashlooping due to OOM on non-drained nodes?
carla (runtime): two pods on 12 are crashlooping; moving them to lower-memory nodes, killing problematic pods to allow redeploy. Using:
```
kubectl delete pod svc-embed-12-xyz --grace-period=0 --force
``` 
ben (sre): note: we saw a single uncorrectable ECC event on 05 earlier but no machine-level panic. We'll capture full nvidia-bug-report from cordoned nodes and attach to ticket.
infra-bot: Generated bugreport: /artifacts/bugreports/3005001234-infer-prod-1-05.tgz
alice (oncall): good. Once bugreport and dmesg are attached, escalate to HW team if uncorrectable counts persist. For now, continue draining and client routing.
todd (prod-eng): next steps for postmortem: identify any runtime config that amplifies GPU memory pressure (prefetch sizes, batch windows) and propose mitigations (dynamic batch caps, graceful degradation).
maria (support): customer bridge open. Two customers on the bridge (cust-A, cust-B) asking for ETA.
alice (oncall): give them current status: mitigations applied, expected stabilization within 30-45 minutes; we'll follow up with a formal incident summary.
carla (runtime): runtime patch deployed to add jittered backoff in restart loop and cap batch size when node health indicates repeatedXid (>5 in 10m). Monitoring now.
ben (sre): metrics after changes: driver-reset rate across pool down 70% in the last 8 minutes. Error rate for embeddings down to 1.2% now.
alice (oncall): great. Keep monitoring 30m. Assign follow-ups: Ben to collect hardware logs and RMA candidates; Carla to author runtime mitigation PR; Maria to draft customer incident update; Todd to own postmortem write-up.
ben (sre): logs and artifact links:
- /artifacts/bugreports/3005001234-infer-prod-1-05.tgz
- /artifacts/bugreports/3005001234-infer-prod-1-06.tgz
- dmesg excerpts uploaded to infra ticket #4321
carla (runtime): PR: https://repo.company/pulls/987 - soft-retry backoff + batch cap
maria (support): customer update posted to bridge. customers acknowledged, asked to receive final postmortem.
alice (oncall): closing notes: incident declared mitigated at 16:27 UTC; keeping nodes cordoned pending RMA scheduling. Will flip incident to postmortem flow after 4h unless regressions.
incident-bot: Incident 3005 status -> MITIGATED (mitigation_time: 3005001620, severity: partial-service-degradation).
